status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Conditions in the slice: six in M1 (hunger, cold, wet, fatigue, a cut, drink) and two in M2 (crushed fingers, queasiness). Each has one felt signature and one trade-off whose actions are all in the slice.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

keys.consumer: tavern and garrison conversation (per visit, capped)
HUD icons and body tells only (never a penalty)
HUD: small text tags beside icons

modifier_contract.aim_rule: Modifiers change sway, tremor, speed and timing only. The aim dot always shows the true aim point.
modifier_contract.combine_rule: Collect every active stage's effects, combine per key by the listed rule, clamp to bounds.

stacking_limit.rule: When more than three conditions push the same key the wrong way, only the three strongest apply; the HUD shows the three most severe condition icons and the journal lists the rest (review 2, issue 7).

modifier_contract.mask_rule: tell_mask hides a condition's icon and body tells; it never removes or halves a penalty. Masks and felt readings that changed mechanics were removed in v3.

stage_rules.one_stage_active: Only the current stage's effects apply (not cumulative with earlier stages).
stage_rules.hud: An icon appears at stage 1 or higher, pulses when the stage worsens and fades after 4 s except at the last two stages. Every condition shows cause, stage and cure text in the journal.
stage_rules.durations: Durations are explicit game days in each row (heal_game_days, duration_game_h); there is no process rule.
stage_rules.design_rule: Each condition has one felt signature effect and one trade-off; conditions are decisions, not upkeep timers. Nothing is hidden: tells and pips show every illness once it has effects.

conditions.name: Hunger
conditions.signature: stamina recovers slower, then the hands shake
conditions.trade_off: eat now, or save the provisions for the trail

tell.audio: stomach growl at hungry and worse

conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: 'starvation shouldn't be a thing because of fasting, people can fast for days', then 'I don't like the shaky aim, less stamina and feeling the cold ... skill level should be based on the player, not the game, and their management'. Hunger has no effect on the body, the aim, the skills or the warmth: it only caps and runs down the well-rested boost and slows the refill while resting (SurvivalBridge.REST_CAP_H, REST_DRAIN; SurvivalSleep.REST_FILL_FOOD). The stages stay for the HUD and the notices.

conditions.name: Cold
conditions.signature: the aim trembles and fingers fumble
conditions.trade_off: push on with the work (the woodpile, later the trap line), or stop and make fire
conditions.cure: fire, shelter, dry clothes, food, movement
conditions.period_view: Cold was the one ailment caused directly by weather (K:9).
conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: 'aim should not be affected, adrenaline comes into play' and 'skill level should be based on the player, not the game'. The cold takes nothing from the aim, the hands or the skills: it slows the walk and stops the sprint when very cold (the body), and freezing still kills. In the game (SurvivalBridge, LastingChill; user 2026-09-27: 'make hypothermia no dead just a status effect that has lasting damages', 'no death from cold') the cold does not kill: its drain stops at 15 health, and a long cold leaves the player chilled to the bone (health held at 70%, every heal at half speed) until two game days warm and well rested; in extreme cold only a sleep by a heat source rests. The core's own sims keep the freezing death.

conditions.name: Wet
conditions.signature: cold comes faster and the powder may not fire
conditions.trade_off: wade the brook to the far end of the line, or walk round by the log crossing (about 20 game minutes)

powder_dunked.until: powder dried by the fire (60 game min) or replaced

lock_wet_in_rain.prevented_by: a lock cover (backlog item, M3); in the slice, keep the lock under the coat

bowstring_damp.when: rain or fog without a string cover

tell.anim: wade shake-water additive when leaving water

conditions.cure: dry by the fire or in shelter

conditions.name: Fatigue
conditions.signature: the view darkens at the edges and the aim sways
conditions.trade_off: finish the last job before dark (another armload, the last traps), or sleep

conditions.name: Cut
conditions.trade_off: bind it now with your bandage, or finish the job first; hurrying a job doubles the chance of a cut
conditions.balance_note: Balance pass, 24 September 2026 (graph_analysis/survival/survival_balance_report.md): the zone penalty applies in full only while the cut bleeds and at half once it is bound, and a bound cut heals in 1.5-2 game days (about 7-10 days of living at the flow factor). Before, the full penalty lasted 3-3.5 game days: in the simulation harness a working character carried a hand cut at 60-75% of dusks (most from splitting firewood), so fire-making and skinning ran 0.1-0.2 worse all season and the cut was an upkeep timer, not a decision (stage_rules.design_rule).

infection.note: infection and poultices come with the detailed injuries (backlog, M3)

conditions.name: Drink

meter.note: User 2026-09-27 (Vices): a gill 25 and 6 an hour off, so one dram keeps a man merry about an hour, three make him drunk.

conditions.rule: Applies to every character equally; never a trait of any people.
conditions.signature: merry company loosens tongues; every stage costs warmth and steadiness
conditions.trade_off: take a dram by the fire (it feels warm but costs warmth) or in company at the sutler's or the trader's settlement (a little standing and the news), or keep your head for the night and the bargain
conditions.upside: Social: in company (the sutler's store, the trader's settlement) the merry stage adds +1 standing with that community per visit, at most 3 a game month, and opens rumour topics. And from tipsy on, blunt force goes on the bleed pool at half instead of hurting at once (design_note).

stages.danger: Outdoors in winter this is a lethal exposure risk. The time-safety wake rules apply while senseless: a worsening warmth stage wakes the player groggy (needs.json time_safety).

social_rules.merry_standing: In the sutler's store or at the trader's settlement, merry adds +1 standing with that community per visit (cap 3 a game month).
social_rules.no_buff: tell_mask hides icons and body tells only; the masked conditions' penalties still apply. Drink's one bodily effect is on blunt force (design_note).

conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: a little drink is an enhancement: from merry on, blunt force hurts nothing at once, half of it goes on the bleed pool (PlayerWounds), so it is paid later and less; bleeding wounds bleed as ever. Any drink stops the well-rested boost, and so does the hangover (SurvivalBridge.rest_cap_h). Too much (drunk) is when the aim sways and the shots spread; drink takes nothing else from the aim or the skills. The player knows when they are merry and never when they are tipsy, drunk or senseless (the HUD and the notices say nothing past merry). Habit-forming: Vices (dependence, addiction, relapse).

conditions.name: Crushed fingers
conditions.trade_off: bind the hand and keep off the line for a day, or work on one-handed (fine work -0.2, and a second mishap doubles the healing time)

conditions.name: Queasy
conditions.trade_off: eat the doubtful meat now, or go hungry and check the line for fresh

cures.rule: plain grain only (cornmeal, biscuit) until it passes

conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: no aim or stamina penalty. Queasiness keeps its stomach (vomiting what is eaten) and no sprint while vomiting.

conditions.name: Tobacco
conditions.signature: a pipe steadies the hands; too many close together turn the stomach
conditions.trade_off: a pipe before the work or the fight, or keep the twist to sell
conditions.basis: General knowledge: twist tobacco and clay pipes were in every pack and pocket on the 1760s frontier; tobacco was grown in settlers' gardens.
conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: 'tobacco in moderation enhances skills and makes reloading faster a little bit'. Steady (a pipe): skill checks +0.05 and reloads 8% quicker (the game side: FrontierPlayer.reload_time_mult). Heavy (too many pipes close together): queasy as well (cond.queasy, cause tobacco). Habit-forming: Vices (dependence, addiction, relapse). The settlers' crop and pipe: any Native use of tobacco is shown with respect and never as a buff.

conditions.name: Delirium
conditions.signature: jimsonweed madness: visions and voices, the hands and the mind unsure
conditions.trade_off: a leaf smoked for a fever, or more for the visions, at the cost of hours out of your wits
conditions.basis: Jimsonweed (Datura stramonium, 'Jamestown weed'): the soldiers sent to Jamestown in 1676 who ate it in their greens were out of their senses for eleven days (Beverley, The History and Present State of Virginia, 1705).
conditions.design_note: User 2026-09-27: picked jimsonweed among the vices, its trade-off 'keeping to our disaplcine nothing effect aim'. Set by the game side (Vices, stage driven, no meter here): skill checks fail (-0.5), no well-rested boost; told in words when it comes and goes and shown in the Condition tab, nothing on the screen (user: 'just a word notification'); the view and the aim never move.
